## The surface is larger than this card first said — and the first count was wrong for a reason worth recording

Seat: `domain:spec#1` · Session: `session_01UanLVj6xvbS6puBCewLr8L`

### Corrected reading

The disproven rationale — *"the `zod-mirror-parity` ratchet stays at zero drift"* — is not one stray sentence. Scanned whitespace-tolerantly across every `.md` / `.ts` / `.tsx` file in the repo:

| file | occurrences | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts` | **5** | pre-existing source comments, unchanged at merge-base and head — the in-repo text teaching the next author the false rationale |
| `.changeset/5903-objectgantt-declared-keys.md` | 1 | pending; publishes verbatim into the CHANGELOG |
| `.changeset/6051-gantt-flat-config-declared-keys.md` | 1 | pending; publishes verbatim into the CHANGELOG |
| **total** | **7 occurrences across 3 files** | |

Absent control on the same scan: 0.

⇒ **Two** pending changesets publish it, not one, and five source comments assert it inside the very file a mirror author reads while doing the thing the rationale is cited to justify.

### ⚠️ Why my first count said "exactly 1" — a line-anchored grep against line-wrapped prose

The earlier probe was `git grep 'ratchet stays at zero drift'`. These bodies wrap at about eighty columns, and in `5903` the sentence breaks mid-phrase:

```
requiredness — all optional — so the `zod-mirror-parity` ratchet stays at zero
drift for this pair and no `KnownDrift` entry is added.
```

`git grep` matches within a line, so that occurrence was invisible. Re-run whitespace-tolerantly it appears, and the same probe confirms `6051` and the five source comments.

⇒ the line-anchored probe read **1**; the true count is **7**. It missed one occurrence entirely and would have missed any other that happened to wrap.

⭐ The tell that should have caught it sooner: when I pointed a **lit control** at `5903` — a file the gate comment had just quoted as containing the sentence — the control **did not fire**. A control that fails on a file you have independent evidence about is not a null result; it is the instrument telling you it cannot see. I recorded the contradiction rather than resolving it by preference, which is the only reason it got chased.

⚠️ So the 7 above is itself a floor, not a ceiling: it is the count for **one** spelling of the rationale. A paraphrase (`no drift`, `parity holds`, `KnownDrift` framing) would not be matched, and no control here rules that out. Whoever takes this card should widen the spelling before quoting a total.

### What this changes about the card

Nothing about the finding, and quite a lot about its size. The ratchet's blindness is unchanged and still verified from its own source. But the rationale it cannot support is **published in two release notes and asserted five times in the mirror file itself**, so correcting the ratchet's header alone would leave the false claim in every place an author actually meets it.

⛔ Still not a ruling, and ⛔ none of the seven is repaired here: five sit in a file that in-flight PR objectui#9709 touches under a different card, and the two changeset bodies are other cards' published text. PR objectui#9709 removed the **three** occurrences it had added itself (verified: 3 → 0 in its added lines) and now cites this card instead.

<sub>Read at 2026-09-17T18:18Z. Scan taken on the objectui#9606 branch head `d4ba7e3701c0`, whose merge-base reading for the five source comments is identical, so none of the seven is attributable to that PR.</sub>

This card is the **instrument**, not the remediation: the taker makes the blind direction fail and lists what it catches, ⛔ and does not fix what it catches.

⭐ The steady `LedgerName` at **3 → 3** is the control worth explaining, because a naive reading would call it a failure. The identifier's **occurrence count** does not move — the change is *inside* the type:

```
before  type LedgerName = 'KnownDrift' | 'RuntimeOnlyDeclared' | 'UnmirroredDeclared' | 'WiderThanDeclared';
after   type LedgerName =
          | 'KnownDrift' | 'RuntimeOnlyDeclared' | 'UnmirroredDeclared' | 'WiderThanDeclared' | 'MirroredUndeclared';
```

**Four arms → five, one arm added, nothing else in the type touched.** ⇒ ⭐ counting the identifier answers 「is it still referenced in the same places」; reading the declaration answers 「did it gain an arm」. Two different questions, and only the second is the one that matters here — **it is what makes 「no existing ledger moved」 a pin-certified reading rather than the author's assertion**, since all five are now sized by the same AST reader.

The two rising lit controls are expected and not noise: the four-way recognition pin references the pre-existing operators by name, so they grow with it.

## What this card delivered

The **instrument**, ⛔ not the remediation — exactly the stop condition the dispatch set, and satisfied **structurally**: the whole diff is one test file and one empty-frontmatter changeset, so ⛔ no declaration face and no mirror is in it at all.

⭐ The card's thesis in one key, re-verified at this landing's own address: `zod/objectql.zod.ts:283` carries `operators: z.record(…).optional(), // Missing in previous TS scan but common`, and `operators` is absent from the TS `ObjectGridSchema`. **A human noticed the gap at authoring time, wrote it into a comment, and nothing measured it** until this direction existed.

The direction reports **8 entries / 102 keys**, seeded as a FLOOR that can only shrink, with **153 of 161 pairs reading EMPTY** as the non-vacuity control. ⛔ Each remedy — declare the key, or narrow the mirror — moves a published accept set and belongs to its own card at tier.
